clauses.text: The intent of this districts schedule, which contains the regulations for the R5-1, R5-2, R5-3 and R5-4 districts, is to encourage high-rise apartments and mixed-use residential buildings of varied tenures, while also preserving lower density options. [...] For the purposes of the R5 Districts Schedule: [...] Without limitation, applicable Council policies and guidelines for consideration include the Design and Development Guidelines.
below-market rental dwelling units has the meaning set out in Schedule J: Affordable Housing Schedule of this by-law;
low-rise apartment means apartment containing more than 8 dwelling units with a maximum building height of 23.0 m, or with a maximum building height of 27.5 m where;
a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units and the site is in a transit-oriented area, or
100% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing;
low-rise mixed-use residential building means mixed-use residential building with a maximum building height of 23.0 m, or with a maximum building height of 27.5 m where:
a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units and the site is in a transit-oriented area, or
100% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing;
high-rise apartment means apartment containing more than 8 dwelling units with a maximum building height of 84.0 m, or with a maximum building height of 69.0 m in the R5-2 district;
high-rise mixed-use residential building means mixed-use residential building with a maximum building height of 84.0 m, or with a maximum building height of 69.0 m in the R5-2 district; and
transit-oriented area means an area designated as a transit-oriented area under the Transit-Oriented Areas Designation By-law.

The table below provides an overview of the outright and conditional approval uses in the R5-1, R5-2, R5-3 and R5-4 districts, categorized by the minimum site area required, where applicable. Applicable density, form and placement regulations in section 3 of this schedule are cross-referenced in the third column.

All outright and conditional approval uses are subject to all other provisions of this by-law, including Section 2, Section 10 and Section 11, and compliance with the regulations of this schedule including section 2.2. [...] The uses identified in the table below as outright approval uses are permitted in these districts and will be issued a permit. [...] The uses identified in the table below as conditional approval uses may be approved in these districts by the Director of Planning, with or without conditions, if the Director of Planning considers: [...] Uses are listed under their general land use category. Applicable use-specific regulations in section 2.2 of this schedule are cross-referenced in the third column. Cross-references to applicable use-specific regulations are provided for information purposes only and do not form part of this by-law.
the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines; and
the submission of any advisory group, property owner or tenant.
Low-rise apartment, low-rise apartment in combination with townhouse, and low-rise mixed-use residential building must comply with the regulations that apply to:
the R3-1 district if the site is in the R5-1 district;
the R3-2 district if the site is in the R5-2 district; and
the R3-3 district if the site is in the R5-3 or R5-4 districts.
Townhouse containing more than 8 units must comply with the regulations that apply to:
the RM-8A district if the site is in the R5-1 district, except that section 3.1.1.3 of the RM-8 and RM- 8A Districts Schedule does not apply;
the RR-1 district if the site is in the R5-2 district; and
if the site is in the R5-3 or R5-4 districts:
the RR-1 district if it:
requires the demolition, or change of use or occupancy of a rental housing unit on that site, or

would have required such demolition, or change of use or occupancy had a person, during the 3 years preceding the date of application for a development permit, not demolished 1 or more rental housing units or changed their use or occupancy, and
the RM-8A district in all other cases, except that section 3.1.1.3 of the RM-8 and RM-8A Districts Schedule does not apply.
Multiple dwelling containing no more than 8 dwelling units must comply with:
the regulations that apply to the R1-1 district, except that section 3.1.1.3(b)(ii) of the R1-1 District Schedule does not apply; and
section 2.2.6 of this schedule if the site is in the R5-3 or R5-4 districts.
The following uses must comply with the regulations that apply to the R1-1 district:
community care or assisted living facility - class A;
duplex;
duplex with secondary suite;
infill, in combination with the retention of a character house;
laneway house;
multiple conversion dwelling, resulting from the conversion of a character house;
principal dwelling unit with lock-off unit;
single detached house; and
single detached house with secondary suite.

The following uses listed in section 2.1 above may be permitted as a conditional approval use if the Director of Planning considers the impact of the use with respect to nearby sites, parking, traffic, noise, pedestrian amenity and size of facility:
cultural and recreational uses, limited to bowling alley, club, fitness centre, museum or archives, and theatre;
manufacturing uses;
office uses, limited to health enhancement centre and temporary sales office;

retail uses, limited to farmers’ market, grocery or drug store, grocery store with liquor store, liquor store, pawnshop, public bike share, secondhand store, shared e-scooter system and small-scale pharmacy; and

service uses, limited to animal clinic, bed and breakfast accommodation, hotel, laundromat or dry cleaning establishment, motor vehicle repair shop, photofinishing or photography studio, print shop, repair shop - class B, restaurant - class 1, school - arts or self-improvement, school - business, school - vocational or trade, short term rental accommodation or wedding chapel.
In the R5-3 and R5-4 districts, development on any site consisting of 3 or more dwelling units that: [...] is subject to the Rental Housing Stock Official Development Plan.
requires the demolition, or change of use or occupancy of a rental housing unit on that site; or

would have required such demolition, or change of use or occupancy had a person, during the 3 years preceding the date of application for a development permit, not demolished 1 or more rental housing units or changed their use or occupancy,
The Director of Planning may permit more than 1 principal building on a site if the Director of Planning considers the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines.
Low-rise apartment in combination with townhouse may only be permitted if the townhouse building is located at the rear of the site.
High-rise mixed-use residential building may include any non-dwelling use listed in section 2.1 of this schedule.
Accessory buildings customarily ancillary to any use listed in section 2.1 of this schedule, except uses that are regulated by other district schedules, may only be permitted if:
no accessory building exceeds 4.6 m in building height; and
all accessory buildings are located:
at least 3.1 m from the ultimate centre line of any rear or flanking lane, and
at least 0.6 m from the ultimate rear property line.

Any other use that is not specifically listed and defined as a use in Section 2 of this by-law may be permitted if the Director of Planning considers the use to be comparable in nature to the uses listed in this schedule, having regard to the intent of this schedule.

Child day care facility conversion dwelling is subject to the regulations, variations and relaxations that apply to: [...] This section contains density, form and placement regulations organized by use.
single detached house, when the child day care facility conversion dwelling was converted from a single detached house; and
single detached house with secondary suite, when the child day care facility conversion dwelling was converted from a single detached house with secondary suite.
High-rise apartment and high-rise mixed-use residential building are subject to the following regulations.
clauses.section_title: 3.1 High-Rise Apartment and High-Rise Mixed-Use Residential Building

clauses.text: For all R5 districts, developments requiring below-market rental dwelling units or social housing are subject to Schedule J: Affordable Housing Schedule.
In the R5-1 district, for high-rise apartment, if the form of tenure for the residential floor area:
is secured as 100% residential rental tenure, the maximum floor space ratio is 6.50 if:
a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units, or
100% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing; or
includes any tenure other than residential rental tenure, the maximum floor space ratio is 5.00 if a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing.

In the R5-1 district, for high-rise mixed-use residential building, the floor area for non-dwelling uses must be at least 139 m2 for all non-dwelling uses combined, and if the form of tenure for the residential floor area:
is secured as 100% residential rental tenure, the maximum floor space ratio is 6.80 if:
a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units, or
100% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing; or
includes any tenure other than residential rental tenure:
the maximum floor space ratio is 5.30 if a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing, and
the maximum floor space ratio is increased to 6.60 if:

the floor area for non-dwelling uses includes a child day care facility that has indoor floor area of at least 464 m2 preserved in the public domain by way of a registered agreement and operated by the City or its delegates, and
a minimum 20% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing.
In the R5-2 district, for high-rise apartment:
the form of tenure for the residential floor area must be secured as 100% residential rental tenure; and
the maximum floor space ratio is 5.50 if:
a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units, or
100% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing.
In the R5-2 district, for high-rise mixed-use residential building, the floor area for non-dwelling uses must be at least 139 m2 for all non-dwelling uses combined and:
the form of tenure for the residential floor area must be secured as 100% residential rental tenure; and
the maximum floor space ratio is 5.80 if:
a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units, or
100% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing.
In the R5-3 district, the form of tenure must be secured as residential rental tenure for 100% of the residential floor area for developments that:
require the demolition, or change of use or occupancy of a rental housing unit on that site, or

would have required such demolition, or change of use or occupancy had a person, during the 3 years preceding the date of application for a development permit, not demolished 1 or more rental housing units or changed their use or occupancy.
In the R5-3 district, for high-rise apartment, if the form of tenure for the residential floor area:
is secured as 100% residential rental tenure, the maximum floor space ratio is 6.50 if:
a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units, or
100% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing; or
includes any tenure other than residential rental tenure, the maximum floor space ratio is 6.00 if a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing.

In the R5-3 district, for high-rise mixed-use residential building, the floor area for non-dwelling uses must be at least 139 m2 for all non-dwelling uses combined, and if the form of tenure for the residential floor area:
is secured as 100% residential rental tenure, the maximum floor space ratio is 6.80 if:
a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units, or
100% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing; or
includes any tenure other than residential rental tenure, the maximum floor space ratio is 6.30 if a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing.
In the R5-4 district:
the form of tenure for the residential floor area must be secured as 100% residential rental tenure; and

the maximum floor space ratio is: [...] if a minimum of 20% of the residential floor area is secured as below-market rental dwelling units or 100% of the residential floor area is developed as social housing.
6.50 for high-rise apartment, and
6.80 for high-rise mixed-use residential building, provided that the floor area for non-dwelling uses must be at least 139 m2 for all non-dwelling uses combined,
